properties.summary: Incident Type: FIXED - NRC Report ID: 835103 - Medium Affected: WATER - Suspected Responsible Party: ISC KETCHIKAN
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 835103
Incident Time: 2007-05-11 14:05:00
Nearest City: Ketchikan, AK
Incident Type: FIXED
Material: SEWAGE
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: ISC KETCHIKAN
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 20 gallons
INFORMATION RECEIVED VIA WEB REPORT: CGC ANTHONY PETIT SUCCESSFULLY PUMPED OFF THEIR SEWAGE & GRAY WATER TANKS THROUGH ISC KETCHIKAN'S SHORE TIE SYSTEMS. AT THE CONCLUSION OF THEIR PUMPING OPERATIONS THE CUTTER ROUTINELY FLUSHES THE SHORE TIE LINES AT A HIGHER PSI TO CLEAN DISCHARGE HOSES BEFORE DISCONNECTING FROM THE SYSTEM. SHORTLY THERE AFTER CREW MEMBERS FROM THE NEIGHBORING CUTTER (CGC ACUSHNET) DISCOVERED LEAKING SEWAGE FROM A VALVE MANHOLE. CGC ANTHONY PETIT WAS NOTIFIED AND FLUSHING OPERATIONS WERE DISCONTINUED. SHORE-SIDE OOD WAS NOTIFIED AND SHORE TIE SYSTEM WAS SECURED. APPROXIMATELY 20 GALLONS OF SEWAGE WAS DISCHARGED DURING THIS FLUSHING OPERATIONS. UPON FURTHER INVESTIGATION IT WAS DISCOVERED THAT THE WRONG SIZE CAP WAS USED TO SECURE THE VALVE FROM PREVIOUS PUMPING OPERATIONS BY THE CGC ACUSHNET. THE WRONG SIZE VALVE CAP WAS REPLACED, PERSONNEL TRAINED, AND SYSTEM WAS PUT BACK IN SERVICE.

properties.summary: Incident Type: PIPELINE - NRC Report ID: 1009271 - Medium Affected: LAND - Suspected Responsible Party: CITGO
properties.content:
Report Details
NRC Report ID: 1009271
Incident Time: 2012-04-20 14:40:00
Nearest City: East Chicago, IN
Location: TANK 53 RECEIPT LINE 2500 EAST CHICAGO AVENUE
Incident Type: PIPELINE
Material: GASOLINE BLENDING STOCKS: REFORM
Medium Affected: LAND
Suspected Responsible Party: CITGO
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 41.628531, -87.439113 (Approximated from street_address)
Reported Spill Volume: 30 gallons
Report Description
AT APPROXIMATELY 2:30 PM ON APRIL 20, 2012 EMPLOYEES AT THE EAST CHICAGO TERMINAL RECEIVED A REVERSE FLOW ALARM FOR TANK 53 FROM THE FUELS MANAGER INVENTORY CONTROL SYSTEM. A LINEUP FOR RECEIVING RBOB FROM EXPLORER PIPELINE HAD BEEN COMPLETED AT ABOUT 2:00 PM BUT THE ACTUAL DELIVERY HAD NOT YET COMMENCED. A FIELD INVESTIGATION OF THE DIKE AREA SURROUNDING TANK 53 WAS COMPLETED AT 2:40 PM AND IT WAS DISCOVERED THAT THE DELIVERY PIPE TO TANK 53 WAS LEAKING A PENCIL THIN STREAM OF RBOB AT THE 6:00 (BOTTOM) POSITION OF THE DELIVERY LINE. BASED ON THE DIMENSIONS OF THE SOIL STAINING AND “FROTH RING” IT WAS ESTIMATED THAT 30 GALLONS HAD BEEN RELEASED. ISOLATION VALVES ON BOTH SIDES OF THE DELIVERY LINE WERE CLOSED WITHIN MINUTES TO ISOLATE THE RELEASE AND FREE PRODUCT WAS REMOVED FROM THE SURFACE VIA VACUUM TRUCK. THE LEAKING SECTION OF PIPE HAS BEEN TEMPORARILY REPAIRED VIA CLAMP CAPABLE OF FULL LINE PRESSURE AND WILL BE REMOVED FROM SERVICE FOR A COMPLETE METALLURGICAL EXAMINATION.

ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION: CALLER IS REPORTING A POTENTIAL RELEASE AND A DERAILMENT OF APPROXIMATELY 8 - 10 RAILCARS AT THE INCIDENT LOCATION. THE DERAILMENT WAS DUE TO UNKNOWN CAUSES AT THIS TIME. CALLER STATED THE TRAIN IS ON FIRE AND A RAIL ROAD BRIDGE HAS COLLAPSED. NO INJURIES WERE REPORTED. DAMAGES COULD POTENTIALLY EXCEED THE $150,000 THRESHOLD. CALLER STATED SOME OF THE CARS DID CONTAIN AN UNKNOWN HAZMAT IN THEM AND IT IS UNKNOWN IF A RELEASE OCCURRED.

VENTURA HARBOR PATROL RECEIVED A REPORT OF A FRESH SHEEN ON THE WATER WITHIN THE HARBOR (PACIFIC OCEAN). THE SHEEN WAS POSSIBLY DIESEL PER THE REPORTING PARTY AND WAS IN THE AREA OF VENTURA WEST MARINA "A" DOCK (1198 NAVIGATOR DRIVE VENTURA, CA 93001). HARBOR PATROL RESPONDED AND COULD NOT LOCATE THE EXACT SOURCE BUT DETERMINED THROUGH WITNESSES THAT IT MAY HAVE BEEN A BI-PRODUCT OF THE SAILING VESSEL "DOLPHIN" IN SLIP A-48 WHICH HAS BEEN SITTING FOR SOME TIME AND RECENTLY LEFT THE MARINA. THE PRODUCT SHEEN IS APPROXIMATELY 15' WIDE AND 2-300' LONG, STRETCHING ALONG THE RIP-RAP. THE PRODUCT IS UNRECOVERABLE PER THE HARBOR PATROL OFFICER ON SCENE GEORGE KABRIS.

PER 49 CFR PART 171.15 B2, IT IS REPORTABLE FOR SUSPECTED RADIOACTIVE CONTAMINATION DURING SHIPMENT.

Skytruth Analysis

Skytruth Minimum Possible Spill Volume: 0 gallons
WHILE WALKING ALONG THE MISSISSIPPI RIVER’S BANK ON DECEMBER 7, 2010 (ALONG THE REVETMENT), SMALL SHEEN CIRCLES WERE OBSERVED ON THE WATER. UPON INSPECTION, IT WAS DETERMINED THE SOURCE MAY BE AN INTERMITTENT SEEP OF LIGHT NON AQUEOUS PHASE LIQUID (LNAPL) GLOBULES RESULTING FROM HISTORIC OPERATIONS AT THE FACILITY. THE SHEEN DISSIPATED QUICKLY AFTER FIRST APPEARING ON THE WATER. A SIMILAR INCIDENT OCCURRED ON NOVEMBER 10, 2010, AND WAS REPORTED TO THE NRC UNDER INCIDENT REPORT # 959615 AND LDEQ SPOC SYSTEM INCIDENT REPORT # GT01 8451.

THE LOCOMOTIVE WAS SHUT DOWN AND IS EN ROUTE TO THE CLIFTON FORGE YARD FOR REPAIRS.
